candidates.why: dxf_free_pair(pair) at 12016 frees both pair->value.s and pair itself (see 512/515). The very next line 12017 passes `name` (copied at 12013) and `dxfname` (strdup'd at 12012) to new_object, so the freed pair is not dereferenced here — but note dxf_free_pair's `pair = NULL` at 516 is a no-op for this caller, so any later path that still reads `pair` after 12016 would be a UAF. Worth flagging as the free site to audit.

If new_object at 12017 returns non-NULL, the inner while loop at 12007 re-tests `pair->code`/`pair->value.s` on the *new* pair, which is fine; but on the path where the inner loop exits and control reaches 12148, `dxf_free_pair(pair)` is called on the pair returned by new_object. If new_object ever returned the same pointer that was freed at 12016 (it does not today, since it calls dxf_read_pair at 8766), this would be a double-free. Reported as a fragile invariant, not a confirmed bug.

new_object (12017) calls NEW_ENTITY/NEW_OBJECT which call dwg_add_object; dwg_add_object reallocs dwg->object (decode.c:5464) and sets dirty_refs=1. `idx` was captured at 12011 *before* the call, and `obj = &dwg->object[idx]` at 12020 is taken after, so this specific line is safe — but the same realloc invalidates any Dwg_Object* held across the call, which is the pattern used throughout the body (blkhdr at 12027/12087/12120/12133).

`blkhdr` comes from dwg_ref_object at 12027 and `_hdr` is derived from it at 12031-12032. dwg_add_handleref at 12034 may call dwg_new_ref -> dwg_decode_add_object_ref, which can grow dwg->object_ref; more importantly the enclosing loop's next new_object reallocs dwg->object. `_hdr` is then dereferenced again at 12036-12038 (ARGS_REF(_hdr->block_entity)) after the call. Stale-pointer-after-realloc risk.

PUSH_HV at 12126 reallocs `_hdr->entities` (common.h:321). `_hdr` itself is a pointer into dwg->object[] obtained at 12122 via blkhdr; if the pool was reallocated by an earlier new_object in this loop, `_hdr`/`blkhdr` are stale and 12126 writes through them. Also `ref` from 12124 is stored into the realloc'd vector.

The condition chain at 12128-12136 re-resolves `blkhdr` at 12133 and `_hdr` at 12135, then dereferences `_hdr->first_entity` at 12136 and writes `_hdr->first_entity` at 12138 after dwg_add_handleref at 12138. Because dirty_refs=1 (12678), dwg_ref_object re-resolves every time, so the pointer is fresh here — but the write at 12138 happens after a call that can realloc the pool, leaving `_hdr` dangling for the LOG_TRACE at 12140-12142.

In the ENDBLK branch, `_hdr` (12091-12092) is written at 12094, then find_prev_entity(obj) at 12100 walks dwg->object[] using `obj->index`/`obj->parent`. `obj` was captured at 12020 from the pool; if any earlier new_object in this loop reallocated dwg->object, `obj` is stale and 12100 dereferences it (find_prev_entity at 6155/6158 reads obj->parent and obj->index).
